label: b/f/h/d/3 input in the original phase, boosted by early m/t/w/z/o
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at t>=2 (none at t=0,1 or at the delimiter; 14 copy-phase steps). The current input carries most of it: b, f, h, d, 3 together hold about 82% of activation mass (6x lift for b), usually on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude depends on prefix context: it is much stronger when the sequence starts with m or t (and less so w, z or o), or has m/t/w in position 1. The top examples are all b/f/3 inputs after an m/t/w-initial prefix. Rate also rises with orig_idx. It does not fire on most other letters or digits, and only weakly on c/q/r/e/y. The in_tok x early-prefix conjunction has low precision (~0.4 on dev), because many b/f/h/d/3 steps in m/t-initial sequences stay below threshold. The context dependence looks additive and graded, not a clean boolean rule.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=m (+4.80), orig0=t (+4.10), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=h (+3.80), orig1=m (+3.25), orig0=w (+3.24), phase=2 & out_tok=m (+2.79). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.63), prev2_tok=- (-4.26), in_tok=m (-4.10), in_tok=s (-4.04).
